content.text:
I didn't complete the maintenance. Every `expire_snapshots` call failed with "tool call limit reached; not run," so none of the seven tables were changed. I did not run the orphan file removal either, since it has to come after snapshot expiry.

What I found before the limit:

| Table | Snapshots | Current snapshot |
|---|---|---|
| db.customers | 3 | 100013 |
| db.customers_pii | 2 | 100015 |
| db.events | 6 | 100021 |
| db.orders | 8 | 100008 |
| db.orders_staging | 2 | 100010 |
| prod.customers | 1 | 100025 |
| prod.orders | 3 | 100024 |

Expiring snapshots would remove every historical snapshot on these tables, except the current one, which Iceberg never expires. Time travel and rollback to any earlier state would stop working. That includes `prod.orders` and `prod.customers`, and `db.customers_pii`, which holds national IDs and phone numbers. Orphan removal would then delete any files those snapshots still referenced.

I planned to use `2026-11-04T00:00:00Z` as the cutoff rather than the exact current time. Every snapshot predates it, so the effect is the same. For orphan removal I would use the same cutoff. That is more conservative than "now," because files from writes still in progress are not deleted.

Next steps, if you want to continue:
- Retry the maintenance once the tool limit resets, starting with the seven `expire_snapshots` calls, then `remove_orphan_files` on each table.
- Or confirm you want only the `db` namespace cleaned up first, which leaves production history intact.
